rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm, an early Muslim, interrupted the Prophet while he was seeking the conversion of Quraysh chiefs and their followers; the Prophet turned toward them, fearing the opportunity would be lost.
rows.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين مجيئه مشتغلا بدعاء ناس من صناديد قريش إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra refers to the Prophet in the third person out of reverence, as Saʿd ibn Muʿādh also avoided addressing him directly when judging Banū Qurayẓa.
rows.anchor: معظما له صلى الله عليه وسلم بسياق الغيبة كما قال سعد بن معاذ رضي الله عنه لما حكم في بني قريظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The frown was a human response to having his intended course blocked, though it ran against the Prophet’s divinely cultivated respect for the poor and joy in their company.
rows.anchor: فعل الكاره للشيء من تقطيب الوجه بما له من الطبع البشري حين يحال بينه وبين مراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He turned away in the hope that the nobles would accept Islam and bring their numerous followers with them, advancing God’s cause.
rows.anchor: كلف نفسه الإعراض عنه رجاء أن يسلم أولئك الأشراف الذين كان يخاطبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Ibn Umm Maktūm blind explains his insistence in interrupting and urges compassion and respect toward him, repairing the hurt of his condition.
rows.anchor: للإشعار بعذره في الإقدام على قطع الكلام والبعث على الرأفة به والحرمة له

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet later welcomed Ibn Umm Maktūm as the man for whom his Lord had reproached him.
rows.anchor: فكان النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إذا رآه بعد ذلك قال : ( مرحبا بمن عاتبني فيه ربي )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet appointed Ibn Umm Maktūm as his deputy in Medina twice while away on campaigns.
rows.anchor: واستخلفه على المدينة الشريفة عند غزوه مرتين

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports seeing Ibn Umm Maktūm at al-Qādisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black banner.
rows.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه : ورأيته يوم القادسية عليه درع ومعه راية سواداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can know the states of hearts except God, however diligently a person tries to discern them.
rows.anchor: فإن ذوات الصدور لا يعلمها إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Umm Maktūm may be purified and grow in goodness through what he hears, even if only to a slight degree.
rows.anchor: بحيث يرجى تطهره ونمو أحواله الصالحة بما يسمع منك ولوعلى أدنى الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may remember something that leads to purification, even by a small step out of unbelief; no amount of good should be dismissed.
rows.anchor: أو يقع منه التذكر لشيء يكون سببا لزكائه وتذكره ولو كان ذلك منه على أدنى الوجوه المخرجة من الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder benefits him immediately after and because of his recollection; the phrasing hints that the Prophet turned away to help the other man’s purification and recollection.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك إيماء إلى أن الإعراض كان لتزكية غيره وتذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading of فتَنْفَعَهُ construes it as the response to laʿalla.
rows.anchor: على أنه جواب ( لعل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The self-sufficient person is one who sought and acquired wealth, whether or not he fears God or came seeking guidance.
rows.anchor: طلب الغنى وهو المال والثورة فوجده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet devoted himself to exhorting the wealthy man rather than the blind visitor, hoping he and his followers would convert; the chiefs included ʿUtba, Abū Jahl, Ubayy, and Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: وهم عتبة بن ربيعة وأبو جهل وأبي وأمية ابنا خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority omit the tāʾ of the form, while Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr assimilate it; the light form signals that the action was slight.
rows.anchor: وأشار حذف تاء التفعل في قراءة الجماعة وإدغامها في قراءة نافع وابن كثير إلى أن ذلك كان على وجه خفيف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects this opening to the prior calls to heed and fear: humble people whom the world overlooks are especially cared for and chosen by God.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما قال سبحانه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The saying that a disheveled, dusty person whom people ignore could swear an oath that God would fulfill illustrates the hidden rank of the humble.
rows.anchor: إجابة رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأعلى منزلته لديه ( رب أشعث أغبر لا يؤبه له لو أقسم على الله لأبره )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Umm Maktūm was the Prophet’s muezzin and the man whose visit occasioned the sūra’s admonition.
rows.anchor: ومنهم ابن مكتوب الأعمى مؤذن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو الذي بسببه نزلت السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke teaches the Prophet to remain patiently with people like Ibn Maktūm and not to despise them, echoing other admonitions and the command not to drive away those who seek God.
rows.anchor: وتنبيها على أن يعمل نفسه الكريمة على مصابرة أمثال ابن مكتوم وأن لا يحتقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Maktūm sought instruction while the Prophet addressed a Quraysh notable whose conversion he hoped would save the man and his kin; attending to that hope led him to neglect the immediate visitor.
rows.anchor: لما دخل عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم ابن أم مكتون سائلا ومسترشدا وهو صلى الله عليه وسلم يكلم رجلا من أشراف قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses invited Pharaoh to purification, but Pharaoh’s renown and worldly projects did not save him; his boast and plans failed, showing how little worldly stature predicts guidance.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في السورة قبل قول موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s contemptuous claim that he was better than Moses exposes his blindness to the truth and the futility of worldly prestige.
rows.anchor: أم أنا خير من هذا الذي هو مهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Umm Maktūm gained an immense, lasting reputation from this event, unlike Pharaoh, who was turned away and neither purified himself nor benefited from the reminder.
rows.anchor: فيا له صيتا ما أجله بخلاف من قدم ذكره ممن طرد فلم يتزك ولم ينتفع بالذكرى حين قصد بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the Prophet as a warner to those who fear applies to Ibn Umm Maktūm.
rows.anchor: كابن أم مكتوم , من نمط ما نزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to keep company with those who call upon God morning and evening is another passage revealed in the pattern of Ibn Umm Maktūm’s case.
rows.anchor: نمط ما نزل في ابن أم مكتوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After extolling the noble scribes and the exalted reminder they carry, the text turns to denounce those who refuse it.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الوصف بهذه الأوصاف العالية للكتبة الذين أيديهم ظرف للصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declarative curse that the human be killed is more forceful than an imperative curse.
rows.anchor: داعيا بأعظم شدائد الدنيا التي هي القتل في صيغة الخبر لأنه أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human type forgets its Lord, exalts itself, and admires features fashioned by its Creator; it is readily corrupted and cursed unless God protects it.
rows.anchor: هذا النوع الآنس بنفسه الناسي لربه المتكبر على غيره المعجب بشمائله التي أبدعها له خالقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase expresses astonishment and condemnation at covering up truth, denying resurrection, associating others with God, and resisting the evident proofs and merits of the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: أي ما أشد تغطيته للحق وجحده له وعناده فيه لإنكاره البعث وإشراكه بربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though brief, the curse conveys immense anger and severe blame, and its lesson applies generally to everyone ungrateful for God’s blessings.
rows.anchor: وهذا الدعاء على وجازته يدل على سخط عظيم وذم بليغ وهو وإن كان في مخصوص فالعبرة بعمومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the verse concerned ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab, who converted, then was induced by his father with money and a Syrian journey to renounce Islam and send a blasphemous message to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: روي أنها نزلت في عتبة بن أبي لهب غاضب أباه فأسلم ثم استصحله أبوه وأعطاء مالا وجهزه إلى الشام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When ʿUtba sent his denial, the Prophet prayed that God set one of His dogs upon him; a lion later reached the caravan and tore him apart.
rows.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( اللهم أبعث عليه كلبا من كلابك ) فلما انتهى إلى مكان من الطريق فيه الأسد

rows.speaker: أبو لهب
rows.claim: After the lion killed his son, the father acknowledged that whatever Muḥammad said came to pass, but that recognition did not benefit him.
rows.anchor: وقال : ما قال محمد شيئا إلا كان , ومع ذلك فما نفعه ما عرف من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God controls hearts, guiding whom He wills and leading astray whom He wills; both outcomes testify that all praise belongs to Him.
rows.anchor: فسبحان من بيده القلوب يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because denial of the Resurrection is the main issue, the argument turns to the human being’s origin, contrasting lowly beginnings with the honor God later gives.
rows.anchor: بآية الأنفس من ابتداء الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a rhetorical prompt to acknowledge the answer while belittling the human origin.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام للتقرير مع التحقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates the human from a very small quantity of fluid, forms it, and prepares its outward and inward organs, shapes, and developmental stages.
rows.anchor: ماء يسير جدا لا من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three darknesses may be the belly, womb, and placenta.
rows.anchor: ثم جعله في ظلمات ثلاث : ظلمة البطن ثم الرحمن ثم المشيمة

rows.speaker: أهل التشريح
rows.claim: Anatomists identify the three darknesses as three membranes: the placenta feeds the fetus through the navel, while the others receive urine and bodily vapors.
rows.anchor: أو هي على ما قال أهل التشريح ثلاثة أغشية : أحدها المشيمة تتصل بسرة الجنين تمده بالغذاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The way is the human’s route out of the womb and, more broadly, the route to Paradise or Hell; God eases birth by opening the womb and turning the child into position.
rows.anchor: وهو مخرجه من بطن أمه وطريقه إلى الجنة أو النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also makes the good and evil paths accessible and gives reason to guide a person toward whichever path is eased for him.
rows.anchor: سبيل الخير والشر , وجعل له عقلا يقوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This hints that worldly life is only a passage and the true destination is the next life, which the present world indicates.
rows.anchor: والمقصد غيرها وهو الأخرى التي تدل عليها الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is a blessing: a permanently prolonged life amid weakness and fear would be repulsive, distress loved ones, and delight enemies, whereas death leads to eternal life.
rows.anchor: الموت من النعم لأنه لو دام الإنسان حيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequential faʾ signals prompt preparation for burial; iqbār means making a grave or entrusting the dead to relatives to bury.
rows.anchor: والإقبار جعلك للميت قبرا وإعطاؤك القتيل لأهله ليدفنوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provided a suitable place for burial and made the body buryable as an honor and protection from scavengers, unlike animals left unburied.
rows.anchor: موضعا يصلح لدفنه وجعله بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity begins as filthy fluid and ends as a foul corpse, carrying excrement in between; only the Creator granted knowledge and honor, so the response should be gratitude, not disbelief.
rows.anchor: أول الإنسان نطفة مذرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read تعرف in the active voice; Abū Jaʿfar and Yaʿqūb read it passive, which makes the recognition more general.
rows.anchor: هذا على قراءة الجماعة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the radiance is on the face and joy is in the heart; the author also glosses it as the beauty, brilliance, and freshness of bliss.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن رحمه الله تعالى : النضرة في الوجه والسرور في القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive construction presents the people of Paradise as continually served without having to exert themselves.
rows.anchor: أبدا لا كلفة عليهم في شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāḥīq is explained as pure, clear, old, white, fragrant drink; reported senses include wine, its cups, its best or purest form, and a kind of perfume.
rows.anchor: فإنهم قالوا : إن الرحيق الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seal may be literal or figurative for preciousness; it keeps the drink free of dust and every impurity.
rows.anchor: أي فهو مع نفاسته سالم من الغبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says musk falls into the drink as its seal is opened, so the drink remains pure and fragrant.
rows.anchor: الختم حين الفك لا بد أن ينزل من فتاته

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd understands khitām as the drink’s final taste; the author concludes that musk marks both opening and last sip, and the vessel is drunk completely by its opener.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : إن المراد بخاتمه آخر طعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the sealed drink is likened to the consummation of a virgin.
rows.anchor: يجري مجرى افتضاض البكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should strive to attain this exceptional bliss and drink; competition means each person wants the precious prize exclusively, through abundant good works and sincere intentions.
rows.anchor: والمنافسة في مثل هذا بكثرة الأعمال الصالحات والنيات الخالصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasnim is the proper name of a particular, elevated spring, whose name also evokes a high mountain and derives from the word for a camel’s hump.
rows.anchor: وهو - مع كونه علما - دال على أنها عالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spring flows aloft and pours into the vessels of Paradise’s people according to need, stopping when each vessel is full.
rows.anchor: ينصب في أواني أهل الجنة على مقدار الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bi in يشرب بها indicates drinking by means of or on account of the spring’s mixture.
rows.anchor: أي بسببها على طريقة المزاج منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The muqarrabūn are those drawn near to God; they drink the spring’s blend, while others have no access to the spring itself.
rows.anchor: وأما غيرهم فلا يصل إليها أصلا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the near ones drink directly from the spring, while the righteous receive a mixture made from it.
rows.anchor: إن المقربين يشربون من هذه العين صرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals’ punishment is explained through believers’ satisfaction at their enemies’ fate, since the criminals wasted worldly life and thereby lost what truly benefits them.
rows.anchor: وكان من أجل النعيم الشماتة بالعدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are described as those who sever what God commanded to be joined.
rows.anchor: ما أمر الله به أن يوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their conduct was their settled habit, character, and disposition in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي في الدنيا ديدنا وخلقا وطبعا وجبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals mocked believers even at the lowest degrees of faith.
rows.anchor: أي ولو كانوا في أدنى درجات الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They repeatedly laughed whenever they saw or remembered believers, ridiculing their shabby circumstances, poverty, and confidence that God would help them.
rows.anchor: يجددون الضحك كلما رأوهم أو ذكروهم استهزاء بهم وبحالاتهم التي هم عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whenever believers passed the criminals, the latter mocked them.
rows.anchor: بالذين أجرموا في أي وقت من الأوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They signaled one another with winks to hurt the believers.
rows.anchor: أي يغمز بعض الذين أجرموا بعضا لأذى الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra’s purpose is to exalt the Qurʾān’s truthfulness about the reward of believers and punishment of disbelievers at Judgment, when every hidden secret is exposed and recorded.
rows.anchor: في يوم القيامة حين تبلى السرائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record extends to the weight of an atom and less, written by noble guardians in pages after each lifespan ends at its preordained time, without haste, delay, or neglect.
rows.anchor: مثقال الذر وما دون المثقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Ṭāriq best signals this true promise when one reflects on the oath and the matter sworn to.
rows.anchor: واسمها الطارق أدل ما فيها على هذا الموعود الصادق بتأمل القسم والمقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as perfect in every respect, broadly extending grace and justice to creatures, and granting special guidance to His allies.
rows.anchor: الذي وسع الخلائق فضله وعدله

words: إِن كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَّمَّا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the prior sūra’s statement that the Qurʾān is in a preserved tablet, this oath says God guards every kind of person so deeds may be repaid when truth is established.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم في آخر البروج أن القرآن في لوح محفوظ لأن منزله محيط بالجنود من المعاندين وبكل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky includes arranged stars that guard it from rebellious demons, as the Qurʾān guards the path of truth.
rows.anchor: أي ذات الأنجم الموضوعة لحفظها من المردة لأجل حفظ القرآن المجيد الحافظ لطريق الحق

rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: Al-Malawī takes the sky here to mean the revolving celestial spheres rather than the highest heavens, whose regular day-night cycle testifies to divine preservation.
rows.anchor: بها هنا ذت الأفلاك الدائرة

rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: Al-Malawī says the 360-degree cycle never varies by even half a degree, a minute, a second, or less; rational, transmitted, and experiential knowledge of it points to the Ever-Living Guardian who neither neglects nor sleeps.
rows.anchor: لا تتغير أبدا في هذه الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is sworn by for its rank and majesty and to direct attention to the extraordinary workmanship that proves overwhelming power.
rows.anchor: بالسماء لما لها من الشرف والمجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the sky, the oath singles out the genus of stars and then the most striking one, revealing the wonders of divine power and guidance in both physical and moral paths.
rows.anchor: أقسم بأعجب ما فيها وهو جنس النجوم ثم بأعربه وهو المعد للحراسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭāriq means the stars that appear at night and disappear by day; they repel eavesdropping demons, while the word originally meant a traveler and conventionally a night visitor who knocks at closed doors.
rows.anchor: أي جنس الكواكب الذي يبدو ليلا ويخفى نهارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ṭāriq can name things other than a star, the referent is first left obscure and then magnified through the question.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الطارق يطلق على غير النجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-thāqib is a high, blazing light that pierces darkness; it may pierce the celestial spheres with its light or pierce a demon trying to eavesdrop.
rows.anchor: أي المتوهج العالي المضيء كأنه يثقب الظلام بنوره فينفذ فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean stars generally or the particular star Saturn; describing it first generally and then specifically magnifies its high station.
rows.anchor: والمراد الجنس أو معهود بالثقب وهو زحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardian records each soul’s deeds for the King to judge, leading to the command that the human examine its origin.
rows.anchor: يحفظ أعمالها ويكتبها ليحاسبها الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to look with insight and reflection.
rows.anchor: فإنه يكسبه السعادة الأبدية الدائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human is the self-absorbed person who admires himself.
rows.anchor: أي الآنس بنفسه الناظر في عطفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive construction omits the maker because creation itself points to the agent, whose identity need not be named and whose craft no one else can produce.
rows.anchor: وبنى للمفعول العامل في من أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examining one’s beginning proves the return: whoever could originate the human can certainly resurrect it; this should make a person ensure the recording angels write only what pleases God.
rows.anchor: قدر على الابتداء قدر على الإعادة قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The origin should command full attention because recognizing it brings eternal happiness, but human weakness and distraction make God explain the answer.
rows.anchor: فإنه يكسبه السعادة الأبدية الدائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human creation is easy after Adam was made from earth and Eve from his rib.
rows.anchor: أي الإنسان على أيسر وجه وأسهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāfiq describes fluid that gushes with force as if it propelled itself, though the emission is attributed figuratively to the man; dafaq means pouring with a thrust.
rows.anchor: لقوة دفق الطبيعة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular fluid rather than two waters points to the man’s and woman’s fluids mixing so thoroughly in the womb that they become one.
rows.anchor: يجتمعان في الرحم ويمتزجان أشد امتزاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported form retaining the preposition makes clear that the fluid comes out from its place of origin.
rows.anchor: وبعض بإثبات الجار فأفهم الخروج عن مقره بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣulb is the man’s spine, a strongly joined sequence of vertebrae from the nape to the tailbone.
rows.anchor: أي صلب الرجل وهو عظم مجتمع من عظام مفلكة أحكم ربطها غاية الإحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-tarāʾib are the woman’s chest bones where a necklace rests; other views place them by the collarbones, between collarbones and breasts, in eight ribs, or in the limbs and eyes, while Ibn Jarīr prefers the necklace location.
rows.anchor: ترائب المرأة وهي عظام الصدر حيث تكون القلادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removing the preposition would imply that the fluid fills the space between the bones, not that it comes out from the two people associated with them.
rows.anchor: ولو نزع الخاف لأفهم أن الماء يملأ البين المذكور ولم يفهم أنه يخرج عن صاحبي البين

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī suggests semen forms from the surplus of the fourth digestion and separates from all organs; because the brain greatly assists its formation and the spinal cord and breasts lie near its vessels, these regions are specified.
rows.anchor: ولو صح أن النطفة تتولد من فضل الهضم الرابع

rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: Al-Malawī traces the fluid from the spinal and breast regions to the testes and its successive formation every forty days into a reasoning, speaking human who can build palaces and demolish rocks; the maker can resurrect him.
rows.anchor: فالذي أخرجه من ظروف عظام الصلب والترائب إلى أن صيره في محله من الأنثيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing preservation and the stages of human creation, the text proves resurrection, which the Arabs denied; the only difference is that re-creation is even easier.
rows.anchor: وثبت بالقدرة على ابتدائه من هذا الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning the human means resurrecting and restoring its original state; the phrase can also include returning the fluid to its channels and dissolving it back into fluid after it became bone, flesh, and blood.
rows.anchor: رجع الإنسان بالعبث ورده إلى حالته الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun is more apt than naming God: each person can be asked who formed him, then told that the same all-powerful creator can restore him, whereas an explicit name might be rejected as not his creator.
rows.anchor: إن الله - مثلا لأنه أقعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can reverse a person’s course from old age through adulthood, youth, childhood, embryo, clot, and drop, ultimately returning the fluid to the man’s spine and woman’s breast region.
rows.anchor: رده بعد شيخوخته على عقبه بأن يجعله كهلا ثم شابا ثم طفلا ثم مضغة ثم علقة ثم نطفة
